deep.reconstruction:
Folio 5r (manuscript p. 9) opens §4, 'Schöpfung der irrationalen Zahlen'. It is the draft of §4 of Dedekind's 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872). That essay, by Dedekind's own account, rests on ideas he formed in November 1858.

Step 1 (motivation). The preceding §3 argued that the continuity of the line is an axiom: a line is continuous if every division of its points into two classes, with every point of the first lying to the left of every point of the second, is produced by exactly one point. The page now says this indicates how the discontinuous domain R of rationals must be completed to a continuous one.

Step 2 (recall of §1). Every rational a determines a partition of Q into two classes A1 and A2:
- A1 = {x in Q : x < a}
- A2 = {x in Q : x > a}
The number a itself may be assigned at will to A1 or to A2. It is then either max A1 or min A2.

Step 3 (abstraction). Compare the elements of the classes only with each other, not with a. The only essential property left is: for all a1 in A1 and all a2 in A2, a1 < a2.

Step 4 (definition, completed on the next page). A partition (A1, A2) of Q with a1 < a2 for every a1 in A1 and a2 in A2 is called a 'Schnitt' (cut). Every rational a then produces a cut.

The continuation (next page) does three things:
- It shows there are infinitely many cuts not produced by any rational. The model example is A2 = {x in Q : x > 0, x^2 > 2} with A1 the rest.
- It declares that each such cut creates a new irrational number alpha = (A1, A2).
- It adds an explicit verification that A1 has no maximum and A2 has no minimum. For a1 >= 1 with a1^2 < 2 it uses a1' = (a1^2 + a1 + 2)/(2a1 + 1), which satisfies a1 < a1' and a1'^2 < 2. For a2 with a2^2 > 2 it uses the Newton step a2' = (a2^2 + 2)/(2a2), which satisfies a2' < a2 and a2'^2 > 2.

This page itself contains no computation, only the conceptual passage from 'cut produced by a rational' to 'cut as an abstract order-partition'.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.

Minor gap, as in the printed text: the definition does not say both classes must be nonempty. Read literally, 'every a1 < every a2' is vacuously satisfied by the trivial partition (Q, empty set); nonemptiness is tacitly presupposed by the word 'Klasse'.
Minor gap: when a rational a is put in A1 versus A2, two formally different partitions arise. Identifying them (the printed text says they are 'not essentially different') is not yet stated here.

results.what: Every rational a induces a partition of Q into {x < a} and {x > a}, with a assignable to either class as its max or min.
Abstract definition of a 'Schnitt': a partition (A1, A2) of Q with a1 < a2 for all a1 in A1 and a2 in A2.
results.modern_name: Dedekind cut; construction of R by cuts

deep.surprise_reason: This is the manuscript draft of §4 of Dedekind's own 1872 essay and matches the published text almost word for word. The cut construction is famously his. Only the draft-level revisions (e.g. reworking the description of the two classes) are of minor philological interest.

checkable.asserts: Next-page check: if 1 < a1 and a1^2 < 2, then (2-a1)/(a1-1) has square > 2, so it is an element of A2.
Next-page check: a1' = a1 + (2-a1^2)/(2a1+1), so a1' > a1 when a1^2 < 2 and a1 > 0.
Next-page check: alternative form of a1'.
Next-page check: the Newton step a2' = (a2^2+2)/(2a2) satisfies a2'^2 - 2 = ((a2^2-2)/(2a2))^2 >= 0.
Next-page check: a2 - a2' = (a2^2-2)/(2a2) > 0 when a2^2 > 2 and a2 > 0.

transcription_corrections: The words struck out after 'nach Belieben der' and in the following line appear to be a cancelled word such as 'kleineren' or 'linken' (reading uncertain), not '[-ersten-]' / '[-oder zweiten-]'. The insertion 'ersten oder der zweiten' replaces them.
In 'die grösste Zahl der [-ersten-] ersten', the struck word looks like 'kleinen' (or similar), not a duplicate 'ersten' (uncertain).
The struck lines at the bottom ('[-[?] Zahl [?]-]') are illegible cancelled attempts. The surviving text reads '...von der Art, dass jede Zahl a1 der ersten Klasse A1', continued on p. 10.
The numeral '9.' at top right is the manuscript page number. The '5' in the right margin is the archival folio number.
